title: Splitting fields of a central simple algebra and similar algebras of the same degree
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file brauer.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The theorem characterizes when a finite field extension splits a finite central simple algebra, namely exactly when some algebra similar to the given one contains the field as a subfield of the maximum possible dimension (statement lines 851-861). The proof is a complete argument: the easier direction identifies the scalar extension of the similar algebra with an endomorphism algebra using a named result on self centralizing subfields (proof lines 863-874); the converse takes the commutant of the algebra inside an endomorphism algebra and uses the Brauer group relation to see that it is similar to the given algebra, then computes its degree by the dimension formula for centralizers and passes to the opposite class (proof lines 876-892). The non-formal content is the identification of the centralizer with the endomorphism algebra and the final dimension count. The claim is H2.
